heading: Lab
title: Make a skill
do: Make the skill you just named.
types:
Write me a skill called [name].
Steps:
1 [...]
2 [...]
3 [...]
Save what we just did as a skill called [name].
Check this skill in [website]. Adapt it.
tip: Then test it: run your skill on a new input.
context: Example lab of the template. Participants work in a folder on their laptop with an AI coding agent (a terminal agent or a desktop app); most are not programmers. Goal: make a skill in one of three ways (write the steps, do the task once and save it as a skill, or adapt a published skill), then test it on a new input in a new session. Common problems: the skill is too big (three steps, one input, one output); vague steps; the skill was saved somewhere unexpected (ask the tool where, and how to run it).
notes: Template lab slide (12d). Copy it for a new lab (slide.py copy live sl-lab --after ID), then describe the lab in DECK_DIR/build/labs.json and run make_lab.py (engage, Lab slides). On screen: the task, the prompt(s) to type, the countdown (Space starts it), the room's status bar and View outputs (the screenshots the room shared). On every phone: Lost / Working on it / Finished, an AI helper that takes a question or a photo of the screen, Share your result (a screenshot for the class), and three next steps on Finished. Needs present mode and the lecturer key; the helper opens when the slide is shown.
